newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban report big battle in northwest Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Taleban report big battle in northwest Afghanistan.

text.p: Heavy fighting broke out between the Islamic Taleban militia and opposition forces loyal to General Abdul Rashid Dostum in northwestern Afghanistan on Thursday, Taleban sources said.

The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press service quoted the sources as saying that Dostum had launched a big offensive on front lines at Bala Murghab, in the remote province of Badghis, in which 1,500 of his fighters backed by warplanes took part.
The sources, contacted at Taleban headquarters in the southern city of Kandahar, said Taleban forces had repulsed the attack after a battle lasting at least seven hours.
Some fighting was continuing, but the front line had not moved significantly as a result of the clashes, which broke a lull in the area that had lasted for more than a month.
The Taleban sources said at least 13 of Dostum's mainly ethnic Uzbek soldiers had been killed and 18 captured. One of Dostum's tanks and three trucks had been destroyed.
Six Taleban fighters were killed and 11 were wounded in the fighting, the sources said.
No independent account of the engagement was available.
The Taleban, battling to impose their purist version of Islam across Afghanistan, advanced into Badghis province a few weeks after seizing the Afghan capital on September 27.
The Taleban's capture of Kabul prompted Dostum to forge a military alliance with his old rival, former government commander Ahmad Shah Masood, against the Islamic militia.
